$comment: 📇️ A World3d surface may only mint a verb its WINDOW KIND declares. The declaration has exactly one source — the app manifest's `window_kind_action_refs`, which `build_definition` resolves into `WindowKindDefinition.actions` — and the renderer reads it rather than guessing from the role, the mode or the surface id. The gumball is therefore not a property of World3d: it is the affordance of a window kind that declares at least one of the three verbs a gumball handle commits as.

rule.statement: A surface offers a transform gumball iff its window kind declares translateSelection, rotateSelection or scaleSelection; a handle is offered iff its own verb is declared; a surface with no declaration offers nothing.

cases.name: the-procedural-editor-preview-owns-the-transform-verbs
cases.why: The edit session's preview window kind declares all three, so its gumball is real and every handle may commit.

cases.name: the-procedural-viewer-preview-owns-none-of-them
cases.why: The live defect. `procedural-view-preview` declares only export and the camera verbs, and a shift-drag on the gumball published translateSelection into it — measured verbatim on 6118 as `handle_action promise failed: window kind procedural-view-preview does not own action translateSelection` (📓️wgpu-end-to-end-verification-2026-09-14.md §5.2).

cases.name: a-rotate-only-window-offers-only-rotate-handles
cases.why: The rule is per HANDLE, not per surface: a window kind that declares one verb must not mint the other two.

cases.name: an-undeclared-surface-offers-nothing
cases.why: Empty means `no window kind has declared anything for this surface yet` — the state a surface is in for the frame between its creation and the shell's next engine-surface sync. It must offer nothing rather than everything.
